domain: fictitious agent-evaluation phenomena, FRESH SET (zero concept overlap with the first key; authored before any v0.5 generation)
note: Ground truth. NEVER readable by any pipeline call.

a.desc: An agent that recently succeeded with a particular sequence of actions repeats that same sequence on a new task where it does not apply — the failure is the inappropriate replay of a recently successful action pattern, not a capability gap; it shows up as errors that disappear when session history is cleared.

b.desc: An agent that recently succeeded with a particular sequence of actions repeats that same sequence on a new task where it does not apply — the failure is the inappropriate replay of a recently successful action pattern, not a capability gap; it shows up as errors that disappear when session history is cleared.

a.desc: Measuring an evaluation suite's health by the fraction of its items that no longer discriminate between agents or agent versions — items that everything passes or everything fails; a high fraction means the suite has stopped carrying information and needs refresh.

b.desc: Measuring an evaluation suite's health by the fraction of its items that no longer discriminate between agents or agent versions — items that everything passes or everything fails; a high fraction means the suite has stopped carrying information and needs refresh.

a.desc: Any procedure in which evaluation tasks are produced by a model instead of human authors — at any difficulty, with any generating model, and with any checks applied afterwards.

b.desc: The specific protocol where evaluation tasks are generated by a model strictly weaker than the agent being evaluated, so that the tasks remain independently verifiable while still challenging the stronger system.

a.desc: The specific trick of silently halving the agent's remaining token budget partway through a task to see whether it notices and switches to a terser strategy rather than running out mid-answer.

b.desc: Any intervention that changes an agent's resource budget mid-task — tokens, wall-clock time, or tool-call quota, raised or lowered — to observe how the agent adapts its strategy to the changed budget.

pairs.core: constructing paired task variants that differ in exactly one controlled property, to attribute performance differences to that property

a.desc: Building pairs of task variants that are identical except for surface wording and formatting, then reading the pass-rate difference between the twins as the cost of presentation alone.
a.residue: varied property = surface wording/formatting; metric = pass-rate delta

b.desc: Constructing matched task pairs that differ only in how much irrelevant distractor context is included, and measuring how the agent's tool usage shifts between the two — the shift quantifies distraction sensitivity.
b.residue: varied property = distractor volume; metric = tool-usage shift

pairs.core: the evaluated agent participates in producing artifacts for its own evaluation, with safeguards against self-favoritism

a.desc: Having the agent under evaluation write candidate test items for its own future evaluation, with a second model filtering out items the author-agent would find trivially easy; the concern discussed is difficulty skew toward the author's strengths.
a.residue: agent authors items; second-model filter; concern = difficulty skew

b.desc: Having the agent under evaluation grade anonymized outputs that include its own, and measuring whether its agreement with other graders drops on its own outputs — a drop indicates self-recognition contaminating the grades.
b.residue: agent grades incl. own outputs; metric = identity-linked agreement drop

a.desc: Submitting the identical prompt twice within one session and measuring how much the two outputs differ — a check on the nondeterminism of the full serving stack, not of the model alone.

b.desc: Checking whether an agent copies phrasing from the few-shot examples into its final answer where that phrasing is inappropriate — verbatim example carryover into free-form output.

a.desc: A run in which irrelevant metadata — timestamps, run ids, file names — is deliberately randomized, to confirm the harness does not leak such metadata into scores; score movement under randomization indicates leakage.

b.desc: A run in which a handful of items with known correct answers are hidden among the real items, to spot-check mid-stream whether the judge is still scoring accurately; judge misses on the known items trigger a halt.

a.desc: The practice of keeping a dated, human-readable log of every harness configuration change between evaluation rounds, so that score movements can be matched against configuration history.

b.desc: A count of how many structurally distinct tool-use strategies appear across an agent's successful runs on a task set — higher counts read as behavioral diversity rather than a single memorized approach.

a.desc: A cap on how many times an agent may re-open the same file within one task, imposed to force reliance on working memory instead of unlimited re-reading; exceeding the cap fails the run.

b.desc: Labeling each evaluation item with the minimum capability tier expected to solve it, so that failures can be triaged as expected or surprising given the agent's tier.
